scope: Bound codec-owned snapshots of source BLOCK_RECORD and canonical LTYPE metadata.

limit.adapterLimits: The three ceilings share the existing basic typed-table adapter policy.

behavior: The estimators account for record-vector storage, common table-entry names, reactors, pending references, XDATA variants, application-data list nodes and payloads, and the BLOCK_RECORD or LTYPE specific strings/vectors.
Const setters validate before copying, stage into temporary vectors, catch allocation failure, clear stale state on rejection and latch a write refusal until corrected.
Move setters validate before consuming caller storage; rejected moves preserve caller data and clear stale codec state.
Successful corrected setup clears only its own rejection state. A setup mutation during an active write marks the write failed without changing the active snapshot.
A rejected snapshot blocks new output before destination publication. The normal adapter limits and low-level setter limits now use the same shared internal constants.

normalFocused.coverage: Exact aggregate item-boundary acceptance, over-limit const and move rejection, caller preservation, stale-data clearing, same-codec correction, injected const-copy allocation failure/retry, and ASCII/Binary destination preservation plus corrected retry across both independent guards.

limitations: The limits estimate logical retained payload and container slots; they do not measure allocator capacity or process RSS.
The two registration vectors have independent 64 MiB ceilings and may coexist in one codec.
Private dxfRW rejection state changes class layout; downstream consumers must rebuild and ABI compatibility remains an open P8 gate.
Other setup assembly/work paths, rollback after earlier staged records, source lifetime, platform numeric/string policies and scoped concurrency remain in the P6 safety audit.
next: Continue the P6 safety audit on other unbounded setup copies and assembly/work paths.
